title: How Basie set the tempo with the rhythm section
summary: Basie noodled at the piano until the tempo was right, with Page, Jones and Freddie Green following him.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Until he gets it just right. It's just like you're fixing a formula, just like you're mixing mash and yeast and everything to make whiskey. You keep tasting it, keep tasting it. A good cake, whatever, you keep tasting it until you get the right ingredients, first. Everything, right to the place where you know it's going to be all right, you know. And he would do that same thing with the piano, noodle and noodle and noodle.
So he really did set those tempos?
Well, now, where does -- you know, in the rhythm section, then, what was the importance of Walter Page and Jo Jones to it?
They kept the tempo he started, you see.

and Freddie Green. They would follow him until he got the right tempo. [And one thing about Basie's band, a lot of people are amazed at how everybody comes in on time, you know. You're finally in the band so long until you know what he's going to play, you see. And then he just noodles and noodles and noodles, he noodles around until he gets it just right.] And then (humming) then you start off.
Well, I mean, I can see that. But Walter Page and Jo Jones sort of --
They kept it where he started it.

Yeah, they knew where it was. They knew where he was going at all times. They knew where he was going. But whichever way the tempo would vary, if it was too flat, too fast, he would bring it down gradually, not abruptly. Nobody would ever know it. Or if it were too slow, he would bring it up a little bit until just right. And when it was right --
